name: Mr. India
summary: Bollywood's invisible man: Arun Verma, a broke violinist who shelters orphans and fights Mogambo with his late father's invisibility device. Played by Anil Kapoor (1987).
origin: Arun is a street violinist who rents a big old house to shelter orphaned children, with help from his cook Calendar, and he is deep in debt. A family friend, Professor Sinha, reveals that Arun's late father, a scientist, built a device that makes its wearer invisible, and that the criminal Mogambo was behind his father's death. Following clues in a letter from Sinha, Arun finds the device in his father's old lab. He starts fighting crime unseen as Mr. India, and the crooks he takes on turn out to be Mogambo's men.
powers: Invisibility from his father's cloaking device
Weakness: visible under red light or through red glass
Otherwise an ordinary, if brave, man

storyline.title: A house full of orphans
storyline.beat: Arun scrapes by to look after the children and takes in journalist Seema as a lodger to pay the bills.

storyline.title: Father's secret
storyline.beat: Arun uncovers his father's invisibility device and learns Mogambo had a hand in his death.

storyline.title: The invisible vigilante
storyline.beat: As Mr. India he rescues Seema when Mogambo's goons catch her undercover, and foils a plan to steal a golden Hanuman idol.

storyline.title: Mogambo strikes back
storyline.beat: To lure Mr. India out, Mogambo plants bombs around the country. One of them, hidden inside a toy, brings heartbreak to the orphanage.

storyline.title: Island showdown
storyline.beat: Captured and taken to Mogambo's island, Arun stops the missile launch. The fuelled missiles explode, the fortress is destroyed and Mogambo dies.

gossip.text: Several publications said the story borrowed from sci-fi films Mr. X (1957) and Mr. X in Bombay (1964). Kapur denied it, saying he never even found copies of them.
The invisibility doesn't work under red light, which is the film's version of kryptonite.
Filming started on 6 July 1985 and took 350 days.
It was remade in Tamil and Kannada in 1989. A 3D sequel was announced in 2011 but never went into production.

quiz.why: The device fails under red light or through red glass.

quiz.q: What instrument does Arun Verma play?

quiz.why: It was the last film written by Salim–Javed.

theme.tagline: You can't punch what you can't see. Unless the lights turn red.

timeline.title: Now you see him
timeline.note: Anil Kapoor's invisible hero arrives in Shekhar Kapur's hit, which stays in cinemas for more than 175 days.

timeline.title: Southern remakes
timeline.note: The story is remade in Tamil as En Rathathin Rathame and in Kannada as Jai Karnataka.

timeline.title: Mr. India 2 announced
timeline.note: Producer Boney Kapoor unveils plans for a 3D sequel. It still hasn't been made.

timeline.title: Sridevi tribute
timeline.note: The London Indian Film Festival screens the film in honour of Sridevi after her death that February.

facts.text: The device fails on red. Under red light or through red glass Arun shows up, and for the red-glass scene he was filmed normally with black paper over the lower frame and a red filter on the lens, then merged with the glass footage.
Kapur reportedly got just ₹10,000 to direct, while Salim–Javed were paid ₹70,000 for story and screenplay.
Satish Kaushik's character Calendar got his name from a dealer who kept using that word, a habit Kaushik heard about from his Delhi-salesman father.
Peter Pereira's team made Arun's footprints with stop-motion and his vanishing with mechanical tricks, since there was no digital VFX in 1987.

Salim–Javed wrote the hero for Rajesh Khanna, then offered it to Amitabh Bachchan, who reportedly asked why an invisible man needed him. The duo took it as an insult and split, and Salim Khan later said he never said they would quit.

Mogambo's line 'Mogambo khush hua' nearly got cut. Kapur wanted several repeats of it trimmed because it came up too often, but Javed Akhtar argued the audience would love it, and it became one of Hindi cinema's best-known lines.
Shekhar Kapur was a comic-book fan who always wanted to make a superhero film and had written several comics himself, including Devi, Snakewoman and The Warlord.
Trade analysts raved so much about Sridevi's performance that some suggested the film's title be changed to Miss India.
Sridevi's scenes dressed as Charlie Chaplin's Tramp took 30 to 35 days to film. She later called them her all-time favourite, and said the crew loved her in the costume.
Anupam Kher was first offered Mogambo, but after his screen test the team thought he looked more funny than fierce. Amrish Puri got the part because his menacing presence suited it.
To play Mogambo, Amrish Puri was told by Kapur to act like a Shakespearean character talking to a nine-year-old child, which is why the villain is grand and scary but still fun.
Mogambo's look was a blond wig and garish knee-high silver boots, a costume that a Times of India writer said had audiences thrilled every time Amrish Puri glared at the camera.
The Encyclopaedia of Hindi Cinema said Mogambo's over-the-top villainy seems inspired by the eccentricities of James Bond villains.
Filmfare named Mogambo the second-most iconic villain in Indian cinema in 2013, and Film Companion, Filmfare and NDTV all listed his catchphrase among famous lines.
A Filmfare writer joked that Mogambo could drop you into an acid tank with the press of a single button, then sign off with his catchphrase. His island lair also holds missiles.
Amrish Puri said Kapur wanted a comic-book villain, not a scary one, and that playing a bad man children loved was great fun.
Seema goes undercover as a Hawaiian dancer called Hawa Hawaii to sneak into a party thrown by Mogambo's henchman Daga, until she is caught and rescued by Mr. India.
Mr. India is called the first mainstream Bollywood science-fiction film, and one critic said it opened the gates to the idea of a superhero for Indian cinema.
Shekhar Kapur picked up the nickname the Steven Spielberg of India, reported by the Glasgow Times, partly because of this film.
Arun looks after ten orphans in the film. Ahmed Khan, who later became a choreographer, and Aftab Shivdasani, who later became an actor, are both listed among the child cast.
Puri's son Rajeev said the actor was asked to say 'Mogambo khush hua' at every award function he attended, and he was offered similar villain roles afterwards.

kidSummary: Arun Verma is a poor violinist who looks after orphans. When he finds his father's invisibility device, he becomes Mr. India and stops the villain Mogambo. Red light is his one weakness.
